properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 28 at 2:01PM MDT until July 28 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 201 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported flash flooding over the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar, with high water and debris flows over
Highway 165 north of San Isabel. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional
rainfall is expected. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will
result in debris flow moving through the North Saint Charles, South
Creek, Squirrel Creek, Middle Creek and North Creek Drainages. The
debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah, Highway 78, stream crossings on Highway 165.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to
Beulah.

properties.description:

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around

outdoor objects is possible.

Locations impacted include...
Montrose.

This includes the following highways...
U.S. Highway 550 in Colorado between mile markers 123 and 130.
U.S. Highway 50 in Colorado between mile markers 84 and 97.
Colorado 90 between mile markers 82 and 89.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 28 at 1:55PM MDT until July 28 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 155 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain fell earlier over
the Buckhorn Creek Basin within the Cameron Peak Burn Scar. Between 1
and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the warning area
will cause debris flows near steep terrain. A debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms in and around the
Buckhorn Creek Basin within the Cameron Peak Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flooding of areas in and around the Buckhorn Creek Basin
within the Cameron Peak Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Larimer County.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Redstone Creek, Eld Creek, North Fork Fish Creek, Buckhorn Creek,
Pennock Creek, Sheep Creek and Cedar Creek.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 28 at 12:56PM MDT until July 28 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Douglas County in northeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 1256 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1.5 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.

the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Larkspur, Greenland and Perry Park.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 28 at 12:13PM MDT until July 28 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive
rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar are possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter Creek and Cutler Creek, particularly along
highway 550, and Cow Creek.

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. Cow creek may also be affected. The debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1202 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gold Mountain Burn Scar, including Cow Creek, and along
highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter Creek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
